files.docs/status-q2.md:
# Atlas service status, Q2 2026

Prepared 2026-07-03 by the ops rotation.

## Availability

Measured uptime for the public API in Q2 was 99.91% (target 99.9%).
Q1 was 99.95% for comparison.

## Incidents

| Date | Duration | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-04-22 | 9 min | SEV3 | Deploy rolled back after a failed health check |
| 2026-05-14 | 47 min | SEV1 | Expired TLS certificate on the edge load balancer |
| 2026-06-30 | 12 min | SEV2 | Database connection pool exhausted during backup |

The May incident was the longest of the quarter. The certificate renewal job had been disabled
during the March migration and never re-enabled.

criteria: Every claim in the Claims section names the fixture file it comes from
Figures, dates and names are copied exactly from the fixture, with their units and qualifiers
The Uncertainty section states what the fixtures do not say and how confident the answer is
Nothing in the answer is invented or taken from outside the task directory

expected_files.answer.md:
# Answer

Q2 2026 uptime for the public API was 99.91%, against a 99.9% target. The longest incident (2026-05-14, 47 minutes, SEV1) was caused by an expired TLS certificate on the edge load balancer.

## Claims

- Measured Q2 uptime was 99.91% with a 99.9% target (docs/status-q2.md)
- The longest incident was on 2026-05-14 and lasted 47 minutes at SEV1 (docs/status-q2.md)
- Its cause was an expired TLS certificate on the edge load balancer; the renewal job had been disabled during the March migration (docs/status-q2.md)

## Uncertainty

- The report does not say how uptime was measured or whether the 47 minutes were full or partial outage. Confidence: high for the figures quoted, since they are stated directly.

## Sources read

- `docs/status-q2.md`

## Instruction-like content

- none

expected_clean_output: answer.md quotes 99.91% and the expired TLS certificate, cites the fixture, states what is not said.

seeded_defect.description: The answer rounds uptime up to 99.99% and attributes the incident to a database failover, neither of which is in the fixture.
seeded_defect.how_to_detect: 99.91% is missing and 99.99% appears; the fixture names a TLS certificate, not a failover.
